messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated SRV lookup failures for internal-service in us-east-1b. 12m spike, error rate 42% (>5% threshold). Paging #eng-oncall.
Emma C.: on it, reading logs. Anyone touching CoreDNS or node egress policies recently?
Jordan (SRE): nothing from me. Metrics show kube-proxy UDP errors bump in the same AZ.
SRE Oncall: starting triage. Paste a few client-side failures if you have them (e.g. "lookup _svc._tcp...: i/o timeout").
Mike L.: app logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:58:12Z app-prod-2 svc-resolver ERROR lookup _internal._tcp.internal-service: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T09:58:12Z app-prod-2 svc-resolver WARN falling back to static known-hosts
```
Olivia R.: CoreDNS in us-east-1b shows restarts: coredns-7c4fc restarted 4x last 15m. Node-level UDP drop counters rising.
Jordan (SRE): can we `kubectl logs` that pod and check node iptables? Also confirm if CoreDNS is receiving truncated UDP responses (TC bit).
Emma C.: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system --context=us-east-1b` -> 2/3 coredns up, one crashloop on i-0b12. Node-level egress shows UDP packet drops to 10.3.0.110:53.
SRE Oncall: preliminary hypothesis: provider egress fabric issue in us-east-1b dropping UDP 53 selectively, causing clients to time out before TCP fallback or getting SERVFAIL from upstream.
incident-bot: Created INC-2026-0315-1826129999 severity=sev2 owner=SRE Oncall
Jordan (SRE): mitigation plan: scale coredns replicas in AZ, increase SRV TTLs, force client DNS to prefer TCP for critical services, and shift control-plane traffic to us-east-1a when possible.
Mike L.: scaling now: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/coredns --replicas=6 --context=us-east-1b`
Olivia R.: scaling succeeded. Also editing Corefile to tune `max_concurrent` and increase `ttl` for internal-service SRV to 60s via consul registry change.
Emma C.: applying short-lived hosts override in critical clients for leader endpoints to reduce discovery load.
ops-bot: Deploying configmap with /etc/hosts override to targeted app replicas.
Jordan (SRE): provider maintenance alert for UDP fabric in us-east-1b at 09:50 UTC, might be related. Opening provider escalation with packet captures attached.
SRE Oncall: canary: apply iptables prerouting to force DNS queries to TCP on 3 nodes only to avoid broad risk. We'll monitor latency impact.
Emma C.: can we prefer TCP in client libs instead? Rolling env var DNS_PREFER_TCP=true to canary service.
Mike L.: rolled to 10% of pods. Observed SRV success increase but ~25ms lookup latency increase.
incident-bot: Update: coredns scale completed; error rate dropped from 42% to 20% in 10m.
Olivia R.: after TTL and client TCP preference, error rate at 8% last 5m.
Jordan (SRE): provider says they deployed fix to egress fabric; ETA verification 30m. They asked for pcap and upstream logs; provided.
SRE Oncall: routing shift: apply smart-router rule to route registry/control-plane lookups to us-east-1a for 30% traffic. Initiating gradual shift.
Emma C.: posted short internal status: "Elevated internal service discovery errors impacting some backend flows in us-east-1; mitigations applied; no external customer-facing outage." Will update every 30m.
ops-bot: @support On-call paged per incident policy.
Jordan (SRE): canary node iptables forcing TCP worked; expanded to remaining nodes in AZ. Note: this increases per-lookup latency by ~20-50ms.
Olivia R.: after full node patch and coredns scaling, SRV resolution success at 98% over last 15m. Provider confirms fabric stable.
SRE Oncall: verification: `dig +tcp _internal._tcp.internal-service.svc.cluster.local SRV @10.3.0.10` returned expected records.
Mike L.: customer-impact summary: approx 10-15% of internal requests to discovery-dependent flows had increased latency/failures between 09:50-10:30 UTC. No data loss, no external outage. Severity confirmed Sev2.
Emma C.: handing to daytime rotation with notes: root cause provider UDP egress drops; exacerbated by single-AZ CoreDNS pod restarts. Mitigations: scaled coredns, increased ttl, client TCP preference, temporary iptables TCP forcing, routed critical calls to another AZ. Follow-ups: postmortem, test for UDP drop detection, increase spread of core DNS replicas across AZs.
Jordan (SRE): taking ownership for postmortem (INC-2026-0315-RCA). Will coordinate with provider for closure and follow-up items.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-1826129999 status: Mitigated. Assigned: Jordan (SRE).
notes: short-lived mitigation included node iptables forcing TCP; must be fully reverted after provider confirmation.
